Article Title: In 1997, Texas researchers poured fluorescein into Dry Fork Sink to map Austin’s hidden aquifer; it travelled at least 4.8 miles to Barton Springs in under 30 hours
Article Text:
Representative image of fluorescent dye tracing the hidden flow of groundwater through limestone aquifers toward a spring. Image Credits: ChatGPT.

A dye trail beneath the city

An underground map made with colour

A fluorescein mixture injected into Dry Fork Sink swiftly made its way to Barton Springs, indicating quick connectivity within the karst structure of the Edwards Aquifer. Image Credits: Wikimedia Commons.

Why Austin's hidden water matters

To understand where water was travelling beneath Austin, researchers used a technique that could make an invisible journey visible. According to the Barton Springs/Edwards Aquifer Conservation District , researchers injected three pounds of fluorescein dye into Dry Fork Sink on June 17, 1997, at 9 am. The sink is located on Kitcheon Branch, a tributary of Williamson Creek, in Sunset Valley, and was used as a natural recharge feature of the Edwards Aquifer. Researchers poured the dye into water entering the sinkhole and later detected it at Barton Springs, demonstrating a rapid underground connection. The report notes that fluorescein was one of several non-toxic organic dyes selected for groundwater tracing because of its suitability and safety for drinking-water supplies and aquatic habitats.The fluorescein travelled underground and was detected at Barton Springs in under 30 hours. The original tracing report gives the minimum distance to the detection point as about 4.8 miles, while an accompanying account puts it at 4.5 miles. Either way, the experiment demonstrated a rapid connection between Dry Fork Sink and the springs. This result mattered because the Edwards Aquifer does not behave like a conventional underground reservoir, where water seeps slowly through tiny spaces between sediment grains.It is a karst system carved into limestone that has fractured and dissolved over geological time. Water can therefore find preferential routes through openings and interconnected conduits, allowing it to travel much faster than might be expected from ordinary groundwater movement.According to research published in the Journal of Contemporary Water Research & Education , a long-distance groundwater-tracing programme began in 1996 and used injected tracers to map groundwater basins and underground flow paths in the Barton Springs segment of the Edwards Aquifer. Results from 40 groundwater traces, 88% of which were successfully recovered, showed that groundwater can move rapidly through the karst aquifer, with mean residence times of about one to eight days. The study found that tracer pulses travelled through conduit pathways far more rapidly than through the aquifer's diffuse-flow component, demonstrating how quickly water can move between recharge areas and springs under suitable conditions.The Dry Fork test was one of many in a broader series that began in the mid-1990s to understand how water enters the aquifer and moves underground before reaching springs or other discharge points. Monitoring equipment was installed at the spring sites and other places where the dye could be found. The activated charcoal receptors proved especially helpful because they could capture traces of the dye, while water samples provided further readings on the tracer. The wider programme eventually identified several groundwater basins within the Barton Springs segment. Traces from parts of the Williamson and Barton Creek watersheds were shown to move toward different discharge points, including Barton Springs and Cold Springs. This replaced assumptions about underground water movement with evidence from water moving through the aquifer.The speed observed at Dry Fork Sink was impressive. Three pounds of fluorescein had to travel at least several miles within less than a day and a quarter. The estimated initial velocity exceeded 21,100 feet per day, but that figure should be treated as a minimum estimate rather than the true speed of water through all underground passages. The water does not follow a simple direct path between sink and spring. The experiment also shows why dye tracing is so useful in a karst aquifer. Underground pathways cannot be identified from surface geology alone. Dye introduced at one point allows groundwater to carry that information downstream.Barton Springs is more than a picturesque landmark. It is a major discharge site in the Barton Springs portion of the Edwards Aquifer and has played an important role in Austin's hydrology for many years. The springs are habitat for endangered aquatic species, so groundwater quality is both a management and ecological issue. That is why the understanding of the groundwater flow paths is so vital. If water can travel from a sinkhole to a spring in hours rather than months or years, contaminants in the recharge area may reach groundwater much faster than expected.Research published in the Journal of Contemporary Water Research & Education also notes that the broader tracing programme demonstrated that rapid groundwater movement is a defining feature of parts of the Barton Springs system. A later synthesis of the tracing work reported that dozens of groundwater traces had been used to delineate flow paths and groundwater basins, with rapid travel times repeatedly observed under suitable conditions. Thus, the Dry Fork Sink experiment made underground flow visible and showed that water entering the sinkhole in the Williamson Creek basin could reach Barton Springs in just a few hours.
Article Summary: Researchers injected three pounds of fluorescein dye into Dry Fork Sink on June 17, 1997, at 9 am. The sink is located on Kitcheon Branch, a tributary of Williamson Creek, in Sunset Valley, and was used as a natural recharge feature of the Edwards Aquifer. Researchers poured the dye into water entering the sink and later detected it at Barton Springs, demonstrating a rapid underground connection.

Article Title: Meet Linus Chen-Plotkin, the 18-year-old Philadelphia student who analysed more than 600 works by Mozart, Beethoven, Haydn, and Schubert and found Mozart's melodies were less predictable
Article Text:
Pic courtesy: Society for Science/Chris Ayers Photography

Teen proves Mozart’s music is unpredictable

Meet Linus Chen-Plotkin

Pic credit: Society for Science/Chris Ayers Photography

Beyond the project

Mozart’s versatility is unparalleled, even today. Ever wondered what made him the ultimate musical architect, with every phrase perfectly placed and every note seemingly inevitable? Well, an 18-year-old from Philadelphia may have found the answer! Linus Chen-Plotkin analysed more than 600 classical compositions and discovered something that musicologists have debated for centuries but never quite quantified. Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart’s melodies are actually harder to predict than those of any other musician, including Beethoven and Schubert.For his Regeneron Science Talent Search project, Linus built three statistical tests to measure something he calls a melody's ‘memory’. His project, ‘Predictability and Statistical Memory in Classical Sonatas and Quartets’, was to find out how much earlier notes influence the ones that come after. The ‘memory’ tracks how much one note depends on the notes before it. High memory means earlier phrases keep influencing what comes next, making it more predictable. Low memory means the composer pivots quickly, keeping listeners slightly off-balance.The teenager ran these tests across 600-plus piano sonatas and string quartets by Joseph Haydn, Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart, Ludwig van Beethoven, and Franz Schubert.What he found was striking. Mozart's music had shorter memory across all three tests, which means his melodies broke patterns faster. They were less predictable. Mozart honoured classical form while constantly slipping something unexpected past the listener's ear. In other words, perfection in Mozart's case didn't mean predictability; it meant something far harder to achieve.Linus’ findings finally provide an answer to understanding Mozart's works. For centuries, critics have thrown around words like ‘genius’ and ‘innovation’ without pinning down what they mean. Linus gave us a way to climb closer to the answer. The unpredictability is what made Mozart the genius he was. An 18-year-old wrestler from Philadelphia picked up statistical tools and told us something new about how Mozart's mind worked. Perhaps Mozart would have enjoyed that twist.Born to Joshua Plotkin and Alice Chen-Plotkin, Linus hails from Philadelphia, PA. He is a student at the Germantown Friends School. He's a varsity wrestler and an advanced Mandarin student. He is not a classical music prodigy who spent his childhood at conservatories, but he knows its mathematics. During the statistical analysis, he approached classical music as a dataset. He saw centuries of musical tradition as raw material for mathematical investigation. He believes his approach and other quantitative methods can help improve the understanding of areas that are typically studied qualitatively. Think music theory, art history, and literature. All these fields have relied on interpretation for centuries, but Linus thinks they don't have to stay that way. Music is not really alien to him. In fact, he also sings and plays blues guitar at The Twisted Tail bourbon bar during his spare time. While he isn’t neck-deep in work, he doubles as a radio operator. Linus is also a licensed amateur radio operator and a former member and soloist of the Philadelphia Boys Choir & Chorale. Few people his age have taken so many different angles on the same art form!Linus isn't stopping at the musical memory. He plans to go beyond. He's collaborating with a Johns Hopkins professor on analysing the grammatical rules of rhyme and metre in Geoffrey Chaucer's medieval poetry. He will be using the same approach on poems that belong to different centuries. The question is almost the same. Can we measure what makes great writing work? Article Title: Nominee vs legal heir: What is the difference and who has claim on assets? All you need to know
Article Text:

Who is a Nominee?



Who is a Legal Heir?

Difference between a Nominee and a Legal heir

Aspect Nominee Legal Heir Role Custodian Owner Transfer of Assets Can be done without any legal formalities. Requires testamentary documents for proof of ownership. Powers No power to transact, use, or transfer assets. Power to use and transact assets as an owner. Appointment Owner can appoint anyone, but some institutions specify certain conditions. Determined by succession/personal laws. Legal Right Cannot contest ownership legally. Can contest ownership in a court of law.

When individuals open bank accounts, invest in mutual funds, or buy insurance, they are often asked to name a nominee.However, many people mistakenly assume that the nominee automatically inherits the assets. In reality, the nominee is not always the final recipient — the ownership rights belong to the legal heir, reported ET.Understanding the distinction between these two is essential to ensure that your wealth is passed on to the intended beneficiaries.A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets.The nominee’s role is limited to holding and managing the assets until they are legally transferred to the rightful heirs.According to ET, the nominee cannot sell, trade, or make any transactional decisions about the assets.The account or policy owner can appoint anyone — family, friends, or acquaintances — as a nominee, though financial institutions often prefer close family members.In some cases, the nominee and the legal heir can be the same person, which helps in ensuring a smoother transfer of assets.The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away.To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will or other testamentary proof.If there is no will — a situation known as dying intestate — the heir is determined as per the country’s succession or personal laws, reported ET.While a nominee can initially access the assets, only the legal heir can claim them permanently or challenge ownership in court.Experts quoted by ET emphasise that having clarity on this difference helps avoid disputes and ensures that the savings reach the intended family members or beneficiaries.Therefore, it is advisable to regularly update both nominees and wills to align with one’s estate planning goals.
Article Summary: A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets. The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away. To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will.

How Jeevan Pramaan simplifies pensioner verification



Every year, lakhs of pensioners across India must prove that they are still alive to continue receiving their pension. This verification, known as the Life Certificate or Digital Life Certificate (DLC), is a crucial and mandatory step in ensuring that pension payments are made only to eligible recipients, preventing fraud and misuse.Traditionally, this process involved visiting the bank or pension office in person, standing in long queues, and submitting a signed paper certificate. However, with the government’s focus on digitisation and technological advancement, this process has become much simpler, faster, and more convenient. Pensioners can now submit their certificates digitally from the comfort of their homes using Jeevan Pramaan, a secure, user-friendly, and Aadhaar-based platform.A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries.The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric-enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.Introduced by the Government of India, it uses Aadhaar-based biometric authentication using either fingerprint or iris scan to verify a pensioner’s identity. Once verified, a digital certificate is automatically generated and shared with authorised pension disbursing agencies.This online process eliminates the need for physical verification, providing elderly pensioners with a simpler and more accessible way to maintain their pension benefits.According to PIB, The submission of the Life Certificate is mandatory for all pensioners who wish to continue receiving their pension without interruption. For the year 2025, the standard submission period is betweenTo make the process more comfortable for the elderly, the government allows pensioners aged 80 years and above to begin the submission process earlier, from 1 October 2025. This extended window gives senior citizens more time and flexibility to complete the procedure without facing last-minute difficulties.The Jeevan Pramaan process involves two main steps: registering the biometric device and generating the digital certificate.Before using the service, pensioners or operators must register their biometric device such as a fingerprint or iris scanner. During registration, the user provides their Aadhaar number and mobile number, after which an OTP (One-Time Password) is sent to their mobile. After entering the OTP, they must provide their name and email ID before scanning their fingerprint or iris.Once authentication is complete, the system confirms that device registration was successful, allowing the user to move to the next step.In this step, the pensioner enters personal details such as Aadhaar number, mobile number, name, PPO number, pension type, sanctioning authority, disbursing agency, and bank account details. The system also asks whether the pensioner has remarried or is re-employed.After entering all details, the pensioner scans their fingerprint or iris using the registered biometric device. Upon successful authentication, the Digital Life Certificate is generated, and an SMS acknowledgment with the Jeevan Pramaan Certificate ID is sent to the registered mobile number.This certificate is automatically stored in the Life Certificate Repository, accessible anytime to both pensioners and pension agencies.Once the Digital Life Certificate is created, it can be electronically delivered to the concerned Pension Disbursing Agency (PDA). PDAs can log in to the Jeevan Pramaan portal to view, verify, or download the certificate directly.Pensioners can also download a PDF copy of their certificate by visiting the Jeevan Pramaan website and entering their Pramaan ID or Aadhaar number. This ensures transparency and easy access for future reference.The government provides several options to submit the Life Certificate, allowing pensioners to choose the method that suits them best.Pensioners who prefer traditional methods can visit their bank branch or a Citizen Service Centre (CSC) to submit their Life Certificate physically. Trained staff at these centres assist pensioners in verifying their details and completing the process.For those unable to travel due to age or health issues, India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) offers a doorstep banking service. Pensioners can schedule an appointment, and an IPPB representative will visit their home to complete the submission using biometric authentication. This service is available for both IPPB and non-IPPB account holders.For pensioners comfortable with technology, the Jeevan Pramaan portal provides a completely online process. By visiting https://jeevanpramaan.gov.in, pensioners can submit their Digital Life Certificate using a computer, laptop, or smartphone equipped with a fingerprint or iris scanner.The system uses the Aadhaar platform to authenticate biometric details. Once verification is successful, a Digital Life Certificate is generated and stored in a secure online repository. Pension disbursing agencies can then directly access the certificate, removing the need for physical paperwork.The UMANG (Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance) app offers another easy option. Pensioners can download the app from the Google Play Store, search for “Jeevan Pramaan,” and select “Generate Life Certificate.”After entering the necessary details such as Aadhaar number, PPO number, and type of pension, pensioners must authenticate themselves using biometric verification. The app then generates a Digital Life Certificate (DLC), which is automatically shared with the pension disbursing authority.All pensioners who receive government, defence, or private sector pensions through authorised disbursing agencies are required to submit their Life Certificate every year. This includes:Failure to submit the certificate within the stipulated period may result in temporary suspension of pension payments until verification is completed.To ensure a smooth submission process, pensioners should keep certain details and documents ready. These include:Having these details ready helps to avoid delays or errors during authentication, whether submitting online or offline.Yes, an Aadhaar number or Virtual ID (VID) is mandatory to generate a Digital Life Certificate. The entire Jeevan Pramaan system is based on Aadhaar authentication, which ensures accuracy and prevents fraud. Pensioners must make sure their Aadhaar is linked with their mobile number and bank account before attempting to generate the certificate.The Digital Life Certificate is fully valid and legally recognised under the Information Technology Act. Pension disbursing authorities across India accept it as an official document, equivalent to the traditional paper-based life certificate.Its biometric verification system makes it secure and tamper-proof, reducing the chances of wrongful pension disbursal or misuse of pension funds.Before the introduction of Jeevan Pramaan, pensioners often faced difficulties in submitting their certificates, especially those with health problems or limited mobility. The digital system has removed these challenges, allowing pensioners to submit their verification anytime and anywhere.By integrating biometric technology and Aadhaar authentication, Jeevan Pramaan has streamlined pension management, improving efficiency for both pensioners and government departments. It also enhances transparency and ensures that genuine beneficiaries receive payments on time.
Article Summary: A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries. The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric- enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.

Go to the official CIBIL website and click on 'Personal CIBIL score,' then 'Get Your Free CIBIL score.' Follow the link provided and fill in all the required details.2. Provide your date of birth, PIN code, and select your state. Finally, enter your mobile number and click on ‘Accept and Continue’.4. Authenticate your identity by entering the OTP (One-Time Password) delivered to your mobile device on the next screen. Click 'Continue' to proceed.5. Choose whether you want to link the device with your account. Select 'Yes' or 'No' based on your preference.6. Upon successful registration, you will see a page confirming that 'You have successfully registered!'7. Click on ‘Go to Dashboard’ to access and view your CIBIL score.The factors influencing the new CIBIL score, as stated on the CIBIL website, include:1. Depth of credit: This refers to the duration of your existing credit history, calculated from the opening date of your oldest credit account.2. Transaction history on credit cards: How you manage transactions on your credit cards impacts your score.4. Number of new accounts opened and number of accounts closed: Opening or closing accounts can affect your score, so managing these actions wisely is important.

Article Title: Dire straits: Brand on the run as Trump suggests Hormuz can be renamed in his honor
Article Text:
Trump’s latest push to rename the Strait of Hormuz adds another chapter to his growing campaign of political branding and geographic renaming

TOI correspondent from Washington:

Donald Trump has rescued a canal, invaded a country, conquered a gulf, annexed a lake -- at least on American maps -- and put his name on a performing-arts center. He now appears to have set his sights on the hottest waterway on the planet.The MAGA boss suggested on his social media account on Wednesday that the Strait of Hormuz could be renamed the “Trump Strait” -- because if you cannot solve a problem, you can at least rename it.The proposal is the latest addition to what has become an extraordinary Trump-era renaming and branding binge. In January 2025, Trump ordered the Gulf of Mexico renamed the Gulf of America for US federal purposes. Last week he signed an executive order changing Lake Ontario to Lake America, saying the US had been treated badly by Canada. He then helpfully suggested that the Atlantic or Pacific could be next, saying, “We have a gulf and we have a lake…Now all we need is an ocean. ”The President, someone jibed, appears to be collecting bodies of water like refrigerator magnets.The joke became even better when Google Maps and Apple Maps fell in line.Google changed Lake Ontario to Lake America for US users over the weekend. Apple followed on Tuesday. Canadians, however, continue to see Lake Ontario and users elsewhere may see both names. In other words, the lake has acquired the geographic equivalent of dual citizenship.The tech companies' compliance prompted criticism from illuminati who argue that private corporations should not allow political pressure to dictate historical and geographic nomenclature. MapQuest, an internet relic many Americans had forgotten existed, refused to make the change and suddenly discovered the most effective marketing strategy in Silicon Valley: stand up to Trump. Its downloads reportedly surged, giving it the kind reception normally reserved for rock bands that haven’t toured for a long time or sports legends making a comeback.There is also an awkward business joke buried underneath all this. Trump built his political persona partly on branding himself as a master businessman, but his corporate record includes repeated failures and bankruptcies in hotels and casinos; His casino empire alone went through multiple Chapter 11 restructurings. Trump-branded ventures have also included products and licensing deals that did not last.Late-night television has naturally treated Trump's naming obsession as premium material. The Atlantic, meanwhile, took the joke to its logical conclusion in a satirical vision of a future America in which everything is renamed “America” or “Trump,” leaving citizens unable to distinguish between brands of products, goods, and structures.Political analysts however see a serious calculation behind what many consider trolling. The renaming campaign sure is presidential theater -- cheap to stage, impossible for the internet and tv to resist, and almost guaranteed to ignite social media. But it also serves to distract people from more pressing issues -- such as cost of living and democracy going down the tubes.
Article Summary: Trump suggested on his social media account on Wednesday that the Strait of Hormuz could be renamed the “Trump Strait” The proposal is the latest addition to what has become an extraordinary Trump-era renaming and branding binge. In January 2025, Trump ordered the Gulf of Mexico renamed the Gulf Of America for US federal purposes.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Tim Cook: “You don't have to choose between doing good and…” - a lesson about ambition, purpose and success
Article Text:
Quote of the day by Tim Cook

“You don't have to choose between doing good and doing well. It's a false choice, today more than ever.”

What Tim Cook means by doing good and doing well

When ambition and responsibility meet

Lessons to learn from Tim Cook’s quote

Stop treating values and ambition as opposites

Think about the consequences of your work

Define success before chasing it

Do not confuse speed with progress

Let principles affect ordinary decisions

How to apply the quote in daily life

Other famous Tim Cook quotes

"Life is fragile. We're not guaranteed a tomorrow so give it everything you've got."

"For the most important decisions in your life, trust your intuition, and then work with everything you have, to prove it right."

"If you embrace that the things you can do are limitless, you can put a ding in the universe. You can change the world."

"History rarely yields to one person, but think and never forget what happens when it does. That can be you. That should be you. That must be you."

A career, a business or even a small personal decision can sometimes create a familiar tension: should success come first, or should doing the right thing? Tim Cook’s quote challenges that assumption. It suggests that achievement and responsibility do not necessarily sit on opposite sides of a decision. For people navigating work, money, ambition and everyday choices, the idea is surprisingly practical. Doing well can mean earning a living, building something useful or progressing in a career. Doing good can mean considering how those choices affect other people. Cook’s point is that the two aims can exist together, provided values remain part of the decision-making process.The quote comes from a 2015 address by Cook at George Washington University, where he spoke about the relationship between personal values, work and professional ambition. His message was directed at graduates entering careers in business, government, science, journalism and other fields. He argued that work does not have to be separated from a sense of moral purpose.“Doing well” in this context is not limited to financial success. It can mean becoming good at your profession, building a stable career, running a successful organisation or creating something that people are willing to use and pay for.“Doing good” is the other side of the equation. It means considering whether the work has value beyond the immediate result. Does it respect people? Does it solve a genuine problem? Does it reflect the principles of the person or organisation behind it?The important part of Cook’s argument is the word “choose”. He is questioning the assumption that these goals must always compete.A person can want a successful career without treating every decision as a purely financial calculation. A company can make money while also paying attention to privacy, accessibility, environmental effects or the way its products affect customers. Those decisions can be complicated, and there are often genuine trade-offs, but the existence of difficult choices does not mean values have to disappear from the process.There is a tendency to interpret statements about purpose as an argument against ambition or profit. Cook's wording does not support that interpretation.People need salaries. Businesses need revenue. Organisations need to remain financially viable if they want to continue employing people or providing services.The point is to widen the definition of success. If someone gets a promotion by undermining colleagues, the promotion may still count as professional progress, but the method matters. If a company grows by misleading customers, the revenue may appear positive while creating another set of costs. If a person earns more by becoming better at a useful skill, there is less conflict between financial progress and personal value.The distinction often lies in how the result is achieved.Ambition is not automatically selfish. Wanting to build a successful career is perfectly compatible with wanting to be fair, reliable and useful.The practical question is what you are prepared to compromise to get there. Before accepting an opportunity, ask not only, “Will this help my career?” but also, “Will I be comfortable with the way I achieved it?”Cook’s later comments about technology and responsibility reinforce this idea. At Stanford in 2019, he criticised the tendency to claim credit for successful outcomes while avoiding responsibility for harmful ones.If you manage people, think about how your decisions affect them. If you sell something, consider whether the customer is getting what was promised. If you publish information, consider whether accuracy has been sacrificed for attention.It is difficult to know whether you are doing well if you have never decided what “well” actually means.For one person, it might mean earning enough to support a family. For another, it could mean becoming an expert, running a company, having creative independence or doing work that has a useful social purpose.Career pressure can make every opportunity look urgent. Yet a quick promotion, larger salary or impressive job title is not automatically the best outcome.Taking a little time to examine an opportunity can prevent years of working towards something that does not fit your priorities.Values are easy to discuss when the decision is large and public. They become more meaningful in routine situations.Reply honestly when a mistake is yours. Give credit to the colleague who did the work. Avoid taking advantage of information someone else does not have. Treat a junior employee with the same basic respect as a senior executive.The idea can be made practical without turning it into a complicated philosophy.At work, aim to become more valuable rather than simply more visible. Build skills that help you and the people around you. If you make a mistake, correct it instead of spending energy protecting your image.With money, earning more does not require abandoning your principles. Look at how you earn, what you buy and what you are supporting with your spending. Financial responsibility and personal responsibility can exist together.In relationships, “doing well” may mean maintaining a healthy, stable life, while “doing good” can be as simple as being dependable. Success becomes less meaningful if it comes at the expense of everyone close to you.Even when making small decisions, there is room for the same test:
Article Summary: Tim Cook's quote suggests that achievement and responsibility do not necessarily sit on opposite sides of a decision. For people navigating work, money, ambition and everyday choices, the idea is surprisingly practical. Doing well can mean earning a living, building something useful or progressing in a career. Doing good can mean considering how those choices affect other people.

"This is to provide LG's position regarding the claims recently raised regarding voice privacy on LG TV's."

The claims made in the recently published video are not true. LG TVs process voice data only when the voice button on the remote control is pressed and held, or when a wake word such as 'Hi LG' is recognized after the user has activated the Far-Field voice recognition feature.

Other than these instances, the TVs do not collect or record ambient conversations. (If the wake word is not recognized, no voice data is transmitted to the server; the audio processing for wake word detection is performed locally on the device and is immediately deleted.)

Additionally, to provide smart TV functionalities, LG TVs feature the ability to scan for and connect to nearby devices on the same network. This is a standard function commonly provided by smart TVs and smart home devices.

The ACR (Automatic Content Recognition) feature is provided on an opt-in basis to deliver personalized content recommendation, services, and advertisements. If a user does not consent to the applicable optional agreement, ACR data is not used for advertising purposes."

Some smart TVs quietly do more than display Netflix and sports scores. According to a new investigation, LG's smart TVs may be among them. A new 135-minute video published by Gamers Nexus on YouTube claims that LG smart TVs continuously sweep home networks, map secondary devices, and log microphone audio while appearing to be turned off.Steve of Gamers Nexus conducted the investigation, working alongside Level1Techs and independent security researchers. Together, they tested retail LG OLED models including the G5. Network packet captures taken through Wireshark showed the TVs actively scanning the local area network for unrelated hardware, including phones and smartwatches.The scanning was not limited to devices on the same network. Apart from internal IP addresses, the sets also gathered the names and signal strengths of neighbouring Wi-Fi networks along with location data, according to the findings.This data pool feeds into LG Ad Solutions, the company's targeted advertising arm. LG claims they have roughly 216 million smart TV sales globally. Meanwhile, the ad division says it has access to 363 million secondary addressable devices in the US alone by tracking other hardware on the same network.The sets also run Automated Content Recognition, or ACR, a system that samples on-screen audio and video into digital fingerprints to log what users watch across inputs.ACR has been well documented on smart TVs in general, but the new testing shows data collection on LG's sets goes much further than that.The more striking finding involved the TV's behaviour when it appeared to be switched off. During bench tests, researchers found the TV could capture clean microphone audio while the screen was, or at least looked to be, powered down in standby mode.The team then tested what happened without an internet connection. When they disconnected the TV from Ethernet, the set continued saving voice input locally and uploaded the stored files once network access was restored, according to the investigation.Beyond the data collection itself, the researchers also documented remote code execution vulnerabilities in webOS, LG's smart TV operating system. Those vulnerabilities are currently moving through the responsible disclosure process, meaning LG has been notified and given time to issue fixes before technical details are made public.Because the TV uses broad network listeners and data sweeps out of the box, the team's recommendation was to disconnect LG sets from the internet and use external streaming devices instead.In a statement, the company said,
Article Summary: A new investigation claims LG's smart TVs collect and store voice data. The company says the claims made in the video are not true. LG claims they have roughly 216 million smart TV sales globally. Meanwhile, the ad division says it has access to 363 million secondary addressable devices.

Article Title: Google launches AlphaGenome Atlas, a map of human DNA: What CEO Sundar Pichai and Google DeepMind chief scientist Demis Hassabis said
Article Text:
Why Google launches AlphaGenome Atlas is significant and it does

Google has unveiled the AlphaGenome Atlas, an extensive, high-resolution digital directory designed to predict how genetic alterations impact molecular biology throughout the entire human genetic sequence. While human DNA comprises roughly 3 billion base pairs, the vast majority of biological research historically centers on 2% that codes for functional proteins. The remaining 98%, often referred to as non-coding regions, has stayed largely uncharted, Google says.Earlier implementations of the underlying AlphaGenome system demonstrated how single-point changes in these non-coding segments can interrupt vital mechanisms like protein synthesis as the broader, systemic picture remained out of reach. To bridge this gap, the newly released Atlas serves as a predictive library detailing the functional consequences of every conceivable single-letter variation across the genetic blueprint.Using the AlphaGenome model, researchers calculated the biological outcomes of all 9 billion single nucleotide changes in advance. The resulting database spans an immense one petabyte of biological information, engineered to let scientific teams run rapid, complex data queries.To keep scientists from drowning in raw information, the platform introduces the AlphaGenome Variant Impact (AVI) score. This singular metric blends forecasts across both coding segments and non-coding sequences, helping laboratory teams pinpoint the most promising leads without manually reviewing thousands of disparate metrics.Google CEO Sundar Pichai said he is excited for what’s to come.“AlphaGenome Atlas is an interactive resource, mapping the predicted impact of all 9 billion DNA variants. It works in a regular web browser, without any coding required, and is free for academic researchers. Excited for the discoveries to come.”Google DeepMind chief scientist Demis Hassabis said: “With AlphaFold we mapped the protein universe - now with AlphaGenome Atlas we’re charting the human genome. It can predict the impact of all 9 billion possible single-letter DNA variants, helping scientists better understand disease. Freely available for academic research”.
Article Summary: AlphaGenome Atlas is designed to predict how genetic alterations impact molecular biology throughout the entire human genetic sequence. The resulting database spans an immense one petabyte of biological information, engineered to let scientific teams run rapid, complex data queries. Google CEO Sundar Pichai said he is excited for what’s to come.
